text:
nina: heads-up — after last night's kernel-selection + batching heuristic deploy (around 00:30 UTC) we're seeing a sharp drop in prefix/prompt cache hit rates on several Private/VPC clusters. p95 token latency OK but token cost and miss-rate spiked for affected tenants.

sam: which deploy/commit? can you paste the deploy bot link?

deploy-bot: deploy complete: ref=feature/kernel-batching-tuning@b4e3f2d by @sam — rolled to all regions (staggered).

irfan: quick telemetry check: Hosted + Dedicated look normal. All failures and hit-rate regressions isolated to Private clusters that have netstore=true (S3-backed KV).
irfan: numbers from one affected customer: hit_rate_before=0.81, hit_rate_after=0.29, median_warmup_time_before=1.1s, after=6.4s.

olga: noticed a keying oddity when I compared computed cache keys from the runtime vs the netstore indexer for the same prefixes — seems like we started normalizing trailing whitespace in the new kernel path but the netstore prefixing pipeline still includes original trailing whitespace -> mismatch.

kevin: that would explain misses (different object keys). is this only for private? why wouldn't Hosted/Dedicated be hit?

irfan: hypothesis: Hosted/Dedicated use local memstore or a different object prefix normalizer. Private customers use our netstore path that prefixes keys with <region>/<tenant> and we introduced url-encoding in that prefix in the new code path. Two incompatible normalizations combined -> misses.

sam: also worth noting the batching change: batch window moved from 3ms -> 6ms and we changed the batching order semantics to prioritize throughput. That reorders request arrivals and the warmup prefetcher relies on ordering to prime the KV. Combined effect = less immediate priming.

nina: paste of small debug snippet from one Private node (truncated):
```
OLD_KEY: tenantA/us-west-2/%20prompt_hash_abc123
NEW_KEY: tenantA/us-west-2/%2520prompt_hash_abc123
// i.e. space encoded as %20 vs double-encoded %2520
```

olga: double-encoding confirmed. netstore indexer expects single-encoding. Runtime change encoded the region prefix twice in some code paths.

kevin: quick mitigations: 1) revert batching window only for Private nodes (feature-flag), 2) add reverse-compat normalization in netstore read path (decode twice if pattern matched), 3) enable aggressive prefetch/warmup for 30m as a stopgap. Which should we do first?

irfan: revert batching flag for Private first (lowest risk), then hotfix normalization in reader. Aggressive prefetch will increase egress/ops cost — use only for impacted tenants.

sam: agreed. I'll flip private batching flag to previous value on the canary pool now and start a controlled rollback for private clusters.

nina: created TKT-4723 documenting regression, root-cause notes and immediate actions (revert flag + reader hotfix + canary). tagging eng-runtime + eng-oncall.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for feature/kernel-batching-tuning on private clusters (canary pool) — rollout id r-2026-11-03-045.

sam: once rollback is in, please collect the same hit-rate samples and post numbers here. we need to quantify delta and keep an eye on any lingering misses from double-encoded keys.

olga: I'll open a small PR with a defensive decode step in netstore reader and a unit test covering double-encoded prefixes.

kevin: long-term fix: unify key-normalization logic in a single library used by both runtime and netstore indexer; add canary tests that compare computed keys across environments.

nina: thanks all — will follow up with perf diffs after rollback. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. keep the thread updated.
